nodes.title: Info about Keyframes / FFLF best practices
widgets_values:
Below you pick an INPUT keyframe type, and an END keyframe type. You can mix and match, starting with a video, ending with a keyframe. Starting with a keyframe, ending with a video. Or sandwitch a gen in between two videos. Play around, it's fun.
Choosing a good strength value is key though! The model will emphasize getting to whichever keyframe has higher strength. If they are both high, you can get jump cuts because the model is being strongarmed in both ends. For shots with a lot of motion in between the start and end keyframes, lower strengths are better.

OmniNFT-RL improves motion and visual fedility. It's the only LoRA I really use.
https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/blob/main/loras/LTX-2.3-OmniNFT-RL-Lora_bf16.safetensors

Notice how each Stage has a sampler_name choice? Feel free to mix and match. euler_ancestral_cfg_pp and res_2s are the two best for the 1st stages, but are slower than some other choices. You can set 2nd and 3rd stages to euler_ancestral if you want a speed up!

If you use a 30XX or even 40XX card, the INT8 model will be 1.2x-1.5x faster than standard fp8 or GGUF. I highly recommend you get the INT8 convrot model and use the INT8 model loader. 
Node: https://github.com/BobJohnson24/ComfyUI-INT8-Fast
Model: https://huggingface.co/bertbobson/ComfyUI-INT8_ConvRot/blob/main/ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-1.1-int8-ConvRot.safetensors
Also, if you don't have sage attention, switch from "disabled" to "auto" below.

Sampler previews. Get the taeltx2_3.safetensors file from:

https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/blob/main/vae/taeltx2_3.safetensors

nodes.title: CLIP Text Encode (Positive Prompt)
widgets_values:
IF you're not achieving good transitions between your keyframes:
1. It could be that your strength values are too high (see sliders to the left). Whichever keyframe input has higher strength will be prioritized by the model.
2. Make sure your prompt accurately describes the motion that is required to get from point A to point B. Often times small details such as description of camera movement can make the difference.
3. You can add prefacing phrases like "a continuous fluid shot from the beginning to end" to your prompts to help guide the model into avoiding jump cuts. Stuff like that might help if nothing else does.
